description: REQ-102's own EARS text establishes a binding invariant -- 'ZERO currently-open loan obligations. Condition (c) is deliberately a single, simple "at most one outstanding loan at a time" rule ... the simplest rule that (i) prevents a citizen from stacking multiple simultaneous loans' (lines 399-405) -- but no mechanism anywhere in REQ-106/REQ-108/REQ-109 actually serializes evaluation of this invariant ACROSS DIFFERENT LENDERS, so a borrower CAN receive two (or more) simultaneously-active loans from two different lenders, directly violating REQ-102's own stated guarantee. The concrete mechanism: REQ-106's own Acceptance Criteria (lines 953-959) states the loan-issuance critical section -- 'REQ-101 read -> REQ-102/104/105 compute -> n = nextLoanSequenceForLender(...) -> disbursement transfer -> ... two-phase ... append' -- is wrapped by `withGigLock(LOANS_LEDGER_PATH, loan_${lenderId}, fn)`. This lock key is scoped PER-LENDER, not per-borrower. REQ-106's own Edge Cases explicitly celebrate this as intentional: 'Two DIFFERENT lenders' loan requests proceed concurrently without contention (different lock keys under the SAME locks/ directory): intentional, not a bug' (line 892), and the Dependencies section states this is a deliberate design choice: 'a precondition THIS feature's own REQ-106 explicitly does NOT have (different lenders intentionally hold DIFFERENT lock keys with zero contention between them)' (line 150). Because REQ-102's own borrower-eligibility check is a PLAIN, UNLOCKED read performed independently by each lender's own issuance flow (it is pure and reads loanRows before that specific lender's own lock is acquired), two different lenders L1 and L2 evaluating the SAME borrower B at nearly the same instant -- or even NOT at the same instant, see below -- can both observe B as eligible (zero 'active'/'defaulted' rows) and both proceed, under their own NON-CONTENDING locks, to disburse to B. This is the exact same architectural hazard class (a lock scoped too narrowly to cover the invariant it's meant to protect) that this SAME spec has already spent three consecutive iterations (FIND-103/FIND-201/FIND-301) hardening for the LENDER side of this exact mechanism -- but the analogous BORROWER-side hazard is never once identified, discussed, or mitigated anywhere in behavioral-spec.md. This is NOT merely a narrow-timing race: because REQ-102's condition (c) only excludes rows with status 'active' OR 'defaulted' -- never 'provisioning' or 'disbursement_uncertain' -- a loan that is issued by lender L1 but left in transient 'provisioning'/'disbursement_uncertain' status (which REQ-106's own text acknowledges can persist for an ARBITRARY duration, since reconciliation for a given lender is only triggered 'at the START of the NEXT loan-issuance attempt for this SAME lender' -- i.e. never, if that lender simply doesn't issue another loan for days) leaves borrower B looking FULLY ELIGIBLE to any OTHER lender for that entire window, not just a millisecond-scale race. Contrast this with `anicca-agent-spawn`'s own analogous MAX_CONCURRENT_SPAWNS=1 precedent, which this spec's own REQ-102 explicitly claims to mirror (line 410, 'mirrors anicca-agent-spawn REQ-102's MAX_CONCURRENT_SPAWNS=1 single-in-flight discipline') -- that sibling feature's OWN Dependencies-cited precedent (`child-spec.js`) achieves its single-in-flight guarantee precisely BECAUSE its upstream caller scopes ALL evaluators under ONE shared 'colony-spawn' lock (this spec's own Dependencies section, lines 144-150, explicitly states this), which is the exact discipline THIS feature's REQ-106 deliberately abandoned in favor of per-lender namespacing -- correctly solving loan_id collision-freedom and lender-surplus protection, but silently discarding the equivalent protection REQ-102's own claimed 'at most one outstanding loan' invariant requires on the borrower axis. No proof obligation in verification-architecture.md tests this: PROP-102c (a static, non-concurrent unit-test fixture) never exercises concurrent evaluation; PROP-106e explicitly tests only loan_id collision-freedom across two different lenders ('produce DISTINCT loan_ids with zero collisions') -- a fixture could satisfy PROP-106e in full while the SAME borrower ends up with two simultaneously-active loans, since PROP-106e asserts nothing about the borrower field at all. As written, an implementation could pass every stated proof obligation in this 48-item document while still allowing a single borrower to receive multiple simultaneous loans from different lenders -- defeating REQ-102's own explicitly-stated safety rule with zero warning anywhere in the spec.

evidence.snippet: Condition (c) is deliberately a single, simple "at most one outstanding loan at a time" rule ... - Two DIFFERENT lenders' loan requests proceed concurrently without contention (different lock keys under the SAME locks/ directory): intentional, not a bug ... The loan-issuance critical section (REQ-101 read -> REQ-102/104/105 compute -> n = ... ) is wrapped by withGigLock(LOANS_LEDGER_PATH, `loan_${lenderId}`, fn)

crossCheck.note: PROP-102c's own test method is a static, non-concurrent unit-test fixture ('fixture with balance $0.01 and one active row for its own borrower_id'). PROP-106e's own test method asserts only loan_id collision-freedom across two different lenders ('assert each lender's own sequence is independent and namespaced ... assert both succeed and their resulting loan_ids are distinct') -- it makes zero assertion about whether the SAME borrower_id could appear as borrower on both concurrently-issued loans. No PROP anywhere in this 149-line proof-obligation table tests cross-lender concurrent issuance targeting the SAME borrower.
